name: Gitea
description: Self-hosted Gitea reads: instance version, token identity, repositories the token can see, one repository's metadata, its issues, and repository search. Read-only; every issue, PR, release and file write endpoint on the same API is deliberately absent.

tools.name: get_version
tools.description: Get the version of the Gitea instance this credential points at

tools.name: get_user
tools.description: Identify the Gitea account the stored access token belongs to

tools.name: list_repos
tools.description: List the repositories the authenticated Gitea account can access

limit.description: Max repositories to return (default 20, capped at 50 by this connector)

tools.name: get_repo
tools.description: Get one Gitea repository's metadata by owner and repository name

owner.description: Repository owner: a username or an organization name

repo.description: Repository name, without the owner prefix

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description: List issues on one Gitea repository, optionally filtered by state, labels or a search term

owner.description: Repository owner: a username or an organization name

repo.description: Repository name, without the owner prefix

state.description: Issue state filter (Gitea defaults to open)

labels.description: Comma-separated label names to filter by

q.description: Search term matched against issue titles and bodies

limit.description: Max issues to return (default 20, capped at 50 by this connector)

tools.name: search_repos
tools.description: Search repositories on the Gitea instance by keyword

limit.description: Max repositories to return (default 20, capped at 50 by this connector)

needs_review: AUTH KEPT AS SCAFFOLDED, AND THE DOCS SAY THE SAME THING: API Usage (https://docs.gitea.com/development/api-usage) documents the token header form 'Authorization: token 65eaa9c8ef52460d22a93307fe0aee76289dc675' for a personal access token, so {type: header, header: Authorization, template: 'token {{token}}'} is unchanged. The vault entry (integrationTypeRegistry.gitea) already sends the identical header in testHeaders, and its testEndpoint is base_url + /api/v1/version, which is this spec's test block verbatim. Gitea also accepts the same token under the Bearer scheme; the documented 'token' form is used because it is what the vault already proves against.

BASE URL IS CUSTOMER-SUPPLIED, SO NOTHING HERE IS PROVABLE BLIND: Gitea is self-hosted, base_url comes from the credential ({fromCredential: 'base_url'}), and there is no vendor-run host to shape-prove against. This spec is NOT SHAPE_PROVEN by a blind 401 sweep; it is marked for the live harness, which stands up an ephemeral Gitea container, creates the admin user 'quoxproof' and a repository named 'quoxproof-live', and drives every tool against it.

CATEGORY: the scaffold wrote 'developer', which is already one of the twelve values in use across this spec directory (cloud_hosting, commerce_finance, communication, crm_sales, data_ai, developer, files_knowledge, hr_hiring, marketing_email, media, monitoring, project_management), and it puts Gitea next to the other source and delivery control planes (github, gitlab, bitbucket, circleci). The vault entry says 'devops', which is not a spec-directory value; 'developer' is its equivalent. Unchanged.

PROBES RESOLVE ON A FRESH INSTANCE, BY CONSTRUCTION: get_version and get_user need no resource at all and carry an empty _probe. list_repos and search_repos answer on an instance with one repository. get_repo and list_issues are the only tools that need an existing resource, and both probe owner='quoxproof' / repo='quoxproof-live', the exact names the live provisioner creates. list_issues probes state='all' so it returns the empty array rather than relying on an issue existing.

LIMIT CLAMP IS OURS AND MATCHES GITEA'S OWN DEFAULT CEILING: Gitea's config cheat sheet documents api.DEFAULT_PAGING_NUM = 30 and api.MAX_RESPONSE_ITEMS = 50, and MAX_RESPONSE_ITEMS is the server-side cap on any paged API response. The 20/50 clamp therefore never asks for more than a default instance will return. It is server-configurable, so the input descriptions say the cap is this connector's, not a hard Gitea fact.

READ-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THE OMISSIONS ARE THE POINT: all six tools are GETs. The same API exposes POST/PATCH on issues, pull requests, releases, repository contents, hooks, teams and org membership, plus DELETE on repositories. None is wired here. Nothing in this connector may be described as managing a Gitea instance.

RESPONSE SHAPES COME FROM THE SWAGGER MODELS: picked fields are Repository (id, name, full_name, description, private, fork, empty, archived, size, language, default_branch, html_url, stars_count, forks_count, open_issues_count, has_issues, created_at, updated_at, owner), User (id, login, full_name, email, is_admin, active, restricted, created, last_login), Issue (id, number, title, body, state, user, comments, created_at, updated_at, closed_at, due_date, html_url) and SearchResults (ok, data[]). /api/v1/user/repos and .../issues answer with a TOP-LEVEL array, hence the '[]' root pick; /api/v1/repos/search wraps its array in {ok, data}. The live harness is what confirms these field names against a real instance.
